balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Legal & General Group plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Legal & General Group plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS here is statutory IFRS 17 earnings per share -- net income divided by the weighted average share count. It is not the measure management guides to.

For Legal & General Group plc: statutory EPS swings with investment variance and one-offs (10.0p FY2025 vs 38.3p FY2022 under the old IFRS 4 basis -- the bases are not comparable). Management and the market instead track core operating EPS (20.93p FY2025, +8.9% YoY; 12.15p H1 2026 vs 10.94p H1 2025), which is steadier and is the DPS cover that matters. The FY2021-FY2025 DPS CAGR is 4.2% (18.45p to 21.79p), broadly tracking core operating EPS growth rather than statutory EPS.

What to watch:

  • Statutory EPS volatility is not a business signal by itself -- check whether it is investment variance or a one-off (Meiji Yasuda gain)
  • DPS growth against core operating EPS growth, not statutory EPS
  • The share count falling as the GBP600m buyback tranches are cancelled

fcf.title: Owner earnings for an insurer
fcf.content:
A conventional free-cash-flow build (operating cash flow less CapEx) does not mean much for an insurer -- operating cash flow is dominated by the timing of premiums, claims and matching-adjustment asset purchases on a GBP580bn+ balance sheet, not by a business's reinvestment needs. There is no owner-FCF series built from the cash-flow statement here.

For Legal & General Group plc: the DCF instead anchors on core operating profit after tax (GBP1,217m FY2025, the "Owner FCF (DCF base)" KPI card above) -- management's own distributable-earnings measure, which strips out investment variance and one-off items (the Meiji Yasuda divestiture gain) from statutory net income. Core debt interest on the Tier 2 and Restricted Tier 1 notes is already deducted inside this number, so no further interest adjustment is made. Net debt is held at zero (the banks/insurers convention): shareholder-level borrowings are matched by what they fund, and consolidated cash is overwhelmingly policyholder and matching-portfolio liquidity, not surplus available to equity holders.

What to watch:

  • Core operating profit growth (target: Institutional Retirement 5-7%, Retail 4-6%, Asset Management to GBP500-600m by 2028)
  • The Solvency II surplus (201% coverage at H1 2026) as the real constraint on distributions, not cash flow

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Legal & General Group plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Legal & General Group plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
An insurer does not report gross/operating profit in the usual sense. The line charted here is statutory net income (IFRS 17 profit after tax).

For Legal & General Group plc: statutory net income (GBP191m FY2024, GBP592m FY2025) is swung around by non-operating items that have nothing to do with the underlying business: the Meiji Yasuda US divestiture gain, and "investment variance" -- the mark-to-market gap between actual and expected investment returns on the annuity book in a given period. Management's own distributable-earnings measure is core operating profit (GBP1,623m FY2025, +6% YoY; GBP918m H1 2026 vs GBP859m H1 2025) -- not yet a chartable CSV column here, but it is the number the DCF's "Owner FCF" KPI card above is built from (after tax). Statutory net income understates the business badly in some years and overstates it in others (the Meiji gain); core operating profit is the steadier line management, equity analysts and this DCF use to value the company.

What to watch:

  • Statutory net income swings versus the much smoother core operating profit trend
  • One-off items: divestiture gains/losses, investment variance, economic assumption changes

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
For an insurer, "revenue" is not premiums collected or investment income earned -- under IFRS 17 it is insurance revenue (the CSM and risk-adjustment release plus expected claims recognised on the in-force book) plus fee income (LGIM's asset-management fees) plus a small other-operational-income line.

For Legal & General Group plc: FY2025's GBP10,511m = insurance revenue GBP9,222m + fee income GBP908m + other GBP381m, continuing operations only. FY2024's GBP12,642m still included the US protection/PRT business sold to Meiji Yasuda (completed 2 Feb 2026), so the YoY comparison across that line is not like-for-like -- FY2025 is the first clean continuing-operations base. Insurance revenue tracks the back book's run-off, not new-business premium volume, so it grows slowly and smoothly; fee income tracks LGIM's assets under management and market levels.

What to watch:

  • Fee income growth (LGIM AUM and flows) versus insurance revenue growth (PRT back-book run-off) -- they are different businesses with different drivers
  • The FY2024-to-FY2025 step down is the Meiji Yasuda divestiture, not organic decline
  • Interim rows show H1/H2 split, not seasonality in the retail-sales sense

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Legal & General Group plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

totalIncome.title: Total income
totalIncome.content:
Net interest income plus fees and other operating income.

For Legal & General Group plc: the top line for a financial; revenue in the ordinary sense does not apply.

What to watch:

  • Income growth versus cost growth
